subject: def-rpm-spacetime-observer-and-worldline

actual_judge.reason: The tetrad definition omits future direction. In Minkowski space, (-e0,e1,e2,e3) is orthonormal and qualifies here, but def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction requires its timelike member to be future-directed. The supplied interfaces therefore conflict.

independent_reason: RPM explicitly adopts the general GR orthonormal-frame convention by saying as in def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields. Its c clause defines a tetrad without a future condition and then defines future-directed as an additional condition; d separately defines observer-adapted. RPM independently requires every observer/congruence/worldline to be future. The sentence pointing to SR says only that the distinctions among charts/frames/congruences agree. It never identifies the larger GR tetrad class with SR(b), which adopts the future-directed subclass. The cited negative-time-leg example is an allowed GR tetrad and is not an observer-adapted tetrad; it refutes no RPM assertion.
scope_preserved: All smooth orthonormal tetrad fields, including ones whose time leg is past-directed. Future-directed and observer-adapted subclasses retain their exact supplier meanings. No new global existence, coordinate-induced or observer-identity claim is introduced.

current_exact_use_excerpts.text: Use the smooth, time-oriented Lorentzian background $(M,g,N)$, signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and the distinct chart, observer, congruence, tetrad and worldline meanings of [[def-rpm-spacetime-observer-and-worldline]]. The metric and time orientation are prescribed data, not dynamical variables. A **charged spinning test body** in this definition consists of the following model quantities along a massive worldline $z:I\to M$:

- The prescribed external electromagnetic field is a $C^1$ alternating covariant two-tensor $F$ on an open region of $M$, independent of the unknown curve. Define $F^\sharp:T M\to T M$ by $g(F^\sharp(v),w)=F(w,v)$. In the flat specialization, a named inertial chart with $x^0=ct$ and $x^i$ in metres uses $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, matching [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]]. On the curved background, $F$ is only a two-form; at an event its components in a chosen orthonormal tetrad use the same algebraic convention. Such a tetrad is a basis field, not a coordinate chart or an observer congruence, as distinguished in [[def-rpm-spacetime-observer-and-worldline]]. The components in an orthonormal tetrad have tesla units. This is an explicit curved-background model input. The cited EM supplier is a flat Minkowski definition and does not derive a curved field or curved Maxwell system.
